dataFileDigests.copy: byte-for-byte from apps/codemap-search/src/redact/pii into the repository-root vendor/ directory, which the existing biome.json already excludes, so formatting cannot rewrite them; the package itself ships only the generated modules
dataFileDigests.embedding: packages/redact/scripts/generate-pii-data.mjs (npm run generate:pii-data --workspace packages/redact) reads vendor/presidio-pii and writes src/pii/data/{catalog,iban-formats,validation-data}.ts as string constants in the formatter's style; the [pii] data-asset test checks the SHA-256 of each embedded string against the pinned digests, so it also runs in the Docker image without vendor/

boundaryTranslation.approach: translateRustRegex() in packages/redact/src/pii/regex.ts; the superset search removes \b as the source does, and the anchored check runs the full translated pattern at the candidate start with the d and y flags
boundaryTranslation.flags: u plus s; i when is_case_insensitive; g for the search and dy for the anchored check
boundaryTranslation.leftBoundary: ^(?:<translated left_boundary>)$ tested on the code point before the candidate
boundaryTranslation.unsupportedConstructs: translateRustRegex throws UnsupportedRegexError; none occur in the catalog

\\b.meaning: Unicode word boundary -> lookaround over [\p{Alphabetic}\p{M}\p{Nd}\p{Pc}\p{Join_Control}]; removed from the superset search

\\B.meaning: Unicode non-boundary -> lookaround alternation over the same word class

\\w.meaning: Unicode word character -> explicit word class

(?i).meaning: inline case-insensitive flag -> dropped; the entry compiles with the i flag

patterns.pattern: Postleitzahl (5 digits, very low base confidence – context required)

rangeConversion.rule: cases.jsonl ranges are UTF-8 byte offsets; the engine reports UTF-16 indices; the tests convert expected byte offsets with Buffer slicing

sweep.method: every entity, detect(text, true) and find(text), best of 2 runs, 19 generic fragments plus up to 18 fragments derived from each entity's first six cases (example + space, example minus last character, example with a trailing é)

worstRatios.verdict: noise: measured while tsc ran; isolated best-of-5 is 4.0 ms -> 16.1 ms (4.0x) and 2 MiB 33.3 ms
sub-millisecond floor; isolated best-of-5 is 0.5 ms -> 1.7 ms (3.4x)

rewrite.before: 16 KiB -> 64 KiB of 'x' took 139 ms -> 2200 ms (15.8x): without \b every start of a long [L.] run scanned to the run end for '@'
rewrite.after: packages/redact/src/pii/accelerators.ts: the leftmost start is the first non-dot of the [L.] run before the first '@' whose local tail and domain match; 'x' x 1 MiB detects in under 0.1 ms; '...@a.b' suffixed inputs stay linear
rewrite.selection: used only while the catalog pattern text equals the one it was written for
rewrite.differential: 80,000 random strings (seeds 1 and 777) compared at every code point cursor in two orders against the translated search regex: 0 mismatches; the suite repeats 5,000 strings
rewrite.otherPatterns: no other pattern needed a rewrite

linearTime.regressionTest: [linear-time] PII patterns grow less than 8x from 256 KiB to 1 MiB: every entity on 'x', '0123456789', 'a@', its first case + space, and its first case with a trailing é; best of 2, re-measured with 5 runs before failing; baselines floored at 1 ms

divergences: Without tree-sitter identifier protection a PII match on an identifier is masked: `const member = sha256;` becomes `const member = ******;` (recorded in the [pii] context test and both READMEs).
Ranges are UTF-16 indices; cases.jsonl byte ranges are converted in the tests.
EMAIL_ADDRESS uses a linear candidate search with the same results as the translated catalog pattern.
The Rust RegexSet prefilter is not ported; each enabled pattern runs its own search, which changes cost, not results.
The application fixture keeps only the 4,500 manifest lines of the five generated sources, as test/fixtures/redaction/pii-app-fields.jsonl with source SHA-256 values in its header.
The source test's final configuration-disable step is not ported; the library has no enable switch.

On Node.js 24 and later (Unicode 17.0), characters first assigned in Unicode 17.0 are letters or digits to the translated \b, \w and \d, while the source's regex-syntax 0.8.11 uses Unicode 16.0; recorded in both READMEs and under rustDifferential.unicodeVersion.

Builds and results go to the OS temp directory.

method: Rust side: rust/ built with regex 1.13.1, regex-automata 0.4.18 and regex-syntax 0.8.11, the versions in the source apps/codemap-search/Cargo.lock (checked on every run), plus byte-identical copies of the source redact/rules.rs and redact/text.rs taken at run time. PII patterns are compiled with the source RegexBuilder options: case_insensitive per entity, multi_line, and dot_matches_new_line.

JavaScript side: packages/redact/dist, with PII patterns built exactly as compilePiiRule builds them (including the EMAIL_ADDRESS candidate scanner) and core results from BUILT_IN_RULES, detectPrivateKeys and detectAssignments.

Compared for each of the 179 PII regex and field_regex entries: the superset search start from every code-point cursor, the anchored candidate (secret or pii_candidate) at every start, and the left-boundary result for every preceding character. Compared for the core: every built-in rule, PEM, and assignment detection range, with and without ENV/INI file paths.

Inputs: the 1,653 pii-cases.jsonl texts, the 4,500 app-fixture texts, 24 seeds for patterns that no fixture reaches, 57 core templates, deterministic mutations of all of them with Unicode digits, whitespace, line breaks, combining marks, case-folding characters and astral characters, and random strings. Characters assigned after Unicode 16.0 are excluded.

Naive control: the same inputs with Rust syntax given to RegExp unchanged must differ from Rust, so a pass cannot come from inputs that miss the semantics that differ. Coverage: every PII pattern must match and every built-in rule id must detect at least once.

unicodeVersion.rustTables: regex-syntax 0.8.11 tables are generated from Unicode 16.0.0 (unicode_tables/perl_word.rs: ucd-generate perl-word ucd-16.0.0).
unicodeVersion.runtimes: Node.js v22.19.0 reports Unicode 16.0; v24.14.0 reports Unicode 17.0.
unicodeVersion.changedCodePoints: 4,700 code points classify differently between the two runtimes for the translator's properties (Alphabetic 4,662, M 42, Lu 28, Ll 27, Nd 10). All but U+0295 were first assigned in Unicode 17.0; U+0295 only became Ll and stays Alphabetic, so word, digit and whitespace decisions for characters assigned in Unicode 16.0 are unchanged.
unicodeVersion.exploratoryRun: Before the tool was committed, a scratch run at scale 5 with seed 1013904223 injected 197 of the changed characters: Node.js 22.19 showed no difference; Node.js 24.14 showed 5,630 core and 791,406 PII result differences, every one in an input containing a changed character. Core detections found only by Rust: 5,740; only by JavaScript: 31.
unicodeVersion.decision: Accepted as a documented divergence in both READMEs (user decision); the tool's inputs exclude characters assigned after Unicode 16.0.

rustDifferential.notCovered: PII validators, context labels, URL quote trimming and IBAN token trimming are code rather than regex; the 1,653 parity cases and the 4,500 app-fixture cases cover them, not this differential.
